items.title: Jim Robinson Interview, 1958-12-10
items.q: Willie Foster, well he was from here... he called me Bob, he said, I said, I'm a good musician. Bob said, man, come on, we'll take a tram on.

ctx.x: Did you join the, that was pretty early, wasn't it? Were you drafted or did you?

No, they drafted. They drafted. Yeah. Yeah. So how did they come pick up trombone? Which the lieutenant was, he wanted the band, you know, for the company. And so he asked them, any fellas had an idea they wanted to take apart in music. Well I knew I could play guitar, but I didn't put no trombone. So they had a fellas from Paulianville, or Onis Heims, he's from Boerleg, he's played in the Claiborne Williams band, well they were a good musician. Willie Foster, well he was from here, and he was a good musician. So…

Bob said, man, come on, we'll take a tram on. We learn you how to play. I said, oh man, I don't want to fool nothing like that. He said, man, you see who done took the raffles from us? He said, no, I said, listen, you got to shovel, you got to pick. You got to handle both them things. You got to dig a hole and shovel all that, that, that. I said, man, that's true, too. He said, look, every day. And we had them big heavy shoes on, and that again, them fellas was in the band, nice, them nice Army Ruskin shoes, you…
